title: Compare First Aid healing after a selector change
changes: Document a bounded injured-character comparison and update the opt-in CH-0226 note to report the observed First Aid healing result.
validation: Protected USA Linux/Xvfb pair used the same injured checkpoint, runtime and inputs; one paused CH-0226 write changed selector 02 to 09. Control and treated copies both healed current HP 65 to 106 with maximum 442, closed normally and preserved guarded inputs. Evidence: dbg20-injured-firstaid-linux-daqpbkda.

Independent protected analysis verified five corresponding screens pixel-identical and all sampled 264-byte first records differ only at offset35 after application. Protected projection regeneration verifies the revised note, unchanged source code lines and other notes. Evidence: dbg20-linux-firstaid-analysis-i5e8wbjf and dbg20-linux-heal-projection-flqixidu.

Three initial attempts using an already-spent turn were stopped on reviewed control screens; no treated case was run. A later interrupted Wine unit left its lease and partial evidence intact; Linux was selected to continue the same criterion without touching it.
limitations: One USA checkpoint and one First Aid use, not a general healing formula, all abilities, native Windows or physical-device equivalence. The interrupted Wine prefix lease still needs coordinated manual recovery.
